text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone who works with it. One key idea is using good naming conventions. Variables and functions should have clear, descriptive names so that other people can quickly see what they do. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time. When code is well organised and readable, developers can fix bugs and add new features without creating new problems.
